messages:
Sam: Seeing a surge of client reconnects from ap-east edge after yesterday's routing tweak. Quotas are getting double-counted in a minute window. Anyone else?
Maria: Yup saw spikes in the console too, a lot of sessions with short-lived SSE disconnects (~8-12s) then immediate reconnect.
Kevin: Logs show servers are not receiving pings but clients still reopen quickly. Could be proxy buffering/stripping keepalives.
Anya: Which change did we deploy exactly? The opaque-proxy routing we rolled out for low-latency routing?
Sam: Yes, rolled to 10% traffic on ap-east: route->opaque-proxy for experimental sticky routing.
Leo: Repro steps? I can try curl from our probe.
Sam: curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.test/stream?session=xyz" and watch connection, we see periodic server-side heartbeat events not observed by client, then client reconnects.
Kevin: Found snippet in server logs: "heartbeat suppressed for session=xyz: proxy reported idle". The runtime suppresses heartbeat when it thinks client is idle to avoid noisy bursts.
Maria: The problem: some proxies (opaque) ack TCP but drop idle comments or strip leading-colon lines. That makes server think client got heartbeat ack, so we stop sending hearts, then proxy silently closes session => reconnect loop.
Anya: Wait, why does runtime rely on receiving client-level acks for server heartbeat? SSE is one-way. Are we using a read-side keepalive from clients?
Kevin: We have a two-way guard: server sends comment heartbeats, expects underlying TCP keepalive or a small client pong header back (legacy hack). Opaque proxy doesn't forward that header.
Leo: That's messy. Two immediate prongs: 1) quick mitigation increase server-side soft timeout + send explicit event that proxies are less likely to drop, 2) add proxy-detection tag in routing and avoid the suppression heuristic.
Maria: For (1) can we switch from comment heartbeats to named event `event: __hb\ndata: 1\n\n` — some proxies treat comments differently. Also bump soft timeout from 10s to 45s for opaque proxied sessions.
Sam: Good. Also we need to surface this in Console: show disconnect reason = "proxy-closed" and flag sessions routed via opaque-proxy so SREs can filter. Right now telemetry lumps everything into generic "SSE disconnect".
Kevin: I'll add metric sse.disconnect_reason.proxy_closed and tag route=opaque-proxy. We'll need to backfill telemetry for last 24h.
Anya: Careful: adding a long timeout increases resource usage; for high QPS endpoints that could increase GPU-side KV cache retention. Need canary and quota safety.
Maria: For rollout UX: do a canary in ap-east 1% with feature-flag holder, wait 1 hour, check disconnect_reason metric and quota billing change. If stable, bump to 25%.
Leo: Also add a small client-side jittered reconnect backoff to avoid synchronized bursts. Clients should at least respect Retry header if present.
Sam: Can we also add server-side logic: if route=opaque-proxy then never suppress heartbeats, and mark session metadata with proxy=true so we can later drop to sane defaults?
Kevin: Yes. I'll open PR to runtime to: change heartbeat format, add route tag, emit metric, and make suppression conditional on route.
Sam: Add test harness that injects an opaque-proxy that strips comment lines. We need automated e2e to catch regressions.
Anya: I'll update the dashboard: per-route heartbeats/missed_acks, session-lifetime histogram, and a small alert if reconnect rate > 0.5% for a 5m window.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: heartbeat-format-hotfix -> canary(ap-east,1%) at 2026-03-18T15:22Z by Kevin.
Maria: Post-deploy check: if we still see duplicate quota charges we may need to change billing to dedupe based on session-id for reconnect windows.
Sam: Agreed, file a follow-up for billing de-dupe. For now prioritize stabilizing sessions.
Kevin: Opening PR now: https://repo.redwood/infra/changes/2345 (contains diff + test harness). Will ping when canary is live.
Leo: Thanks team. Keeping an eye on console metrics.
Maria: One more note — add a small note in rollout doc warning about proxies that compress or normalize SSE payloads. Some CDNs do that and it breaks assumptions.
Sam: Good call. Let's sync after canary results. :thumbsup:
